a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: L1 gold contexts for structurally related heteroaryl-aniline/aminopyrimidine molecules report human absolute oral bioavailability above the 20% threshold: GSK1322322 57% fasted/77% fed, R406 54.6%, ZL-2201 ~70%, brepocitinib 75%, deucravacitinib 99%, and nilotinib 31% fasted.

L2 records reinforce the positive direction: ZL-2201 F was 115% in monkeys and 134% in mice, phenserine rat F was ~100%, brepocitinib is described as orally bioavailable, and cirrhosis contexts for propranolol/isradipine remain above 20%.
Nilotinib's low bioavailability (~31%) is still above the 20% threshold and is attributed to precipitation/incomplete absorption, not a query-specific low-F outcome.

L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal-metabolism records are for other molecules (tandutinib, imatinib, zongertinib, compound 2, diltiazem) and do not provide query-specific F evidence; imatinib is an efflux substrate yet has high oral bioavailability, so efflux alone is not affirmative evidence of F<20.

L6 hepatic clearance/metabolic stability records are for other molecules (M01-M11) and provide no query-specific CLint or F measurement; high HLM CLint values for those compounds are not scaled to hepatic extraction and do not affirmatively establish F<20 for the query.
No active record provides affirmative threshold-relevant evidence of F<20 for the query; the unfavorable physicochemical prior is not endpoint proof.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule; prediction relies on transfer from analog contexts.
No query-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic stability data; L6 records are for other molecules and include species/assay mismatches (rat hepatocytes, mouse/monkey microsomes).
Query-specific isopropyl ester stability/hydrolysis, acrylamide reactivity, solubility/dissolution, and fed/fasted/dose effects are unknown.
Physicochemical liabilities (MW 585, logP 5.08, TPSA 114, low neutral fraction) could reduce absorption but are not affirmative threshold evidence.
